fact: 1924年1月22日，工党领袖拉姆齐·麦克唐纳组成英国历史上首届工党政府，任首相兼外交大臣，内阁成员多数是工人出身。政府为少数派政府，依赖自由党在议会中的支持，但在两院均不占多数。财政大臣菲利普·斯诺登是平衡预算和金本位的坚定拥护者。

sources.title: 快懂百科，英国工党首次执政
sources.quote: 1924年1月22日工党领袖麦克唐纳组成英国历史上首届工党政府。麦克唐纳任首相兼外交大臣,内阁成员多数是工人出身。

sources.title: Biography Guide, Ramsay MacDonald
sources.quote: On 22 January 1924, he took office as the first Labour Prime Minister, the first from a working-class background. ... He consulted widely within his party, making the Liberal Lord Haldane the Lord Chancellor, and Philip Snowden Chancellor of the Exchequer. He took the foreign office himself. ... The Government lasted only nine months and did not have a majority in either House of the Parliament.

fact: 1924年7—8月，麦克唐纳在伦敦召集协约国会议，推动道威斯计划的达成。道威斯计划规定：德国第一年赔款10亿帝国马克，逐年递增到第五年的25亿；美国向德国贷款约2亿美元（8亿金马克）稳定币值；法比军队撤出鲁尔；德国的赔款财源包括关税、烟酒糖专卖税、铁路收入和工商企业税。8月16日各国正式接受道威斯计划，9月1日生效。

sources.title: British Online Archives, 100 Years Since The Dawes Plan Was Accepted
sources.quote: Today (16/08/2024) marks 100 years since the Dawes Plan was accepted by Germany and the Allies. It came into effect on 1 September 1924. ... The plan stipulated that Germany had to resume payment of reparations, beginning with a sum of one billion Reichsmarks in the first year, increasing annually to two and a half billion after five years. ... The USA would loan Germany 800 million Reichsmarks to ensure the stability of the currency. The plan also mandated the withdrawal of troops from the Ruhr.

sources.title: Britannica, A fragile stability 1922–29
sources.quote: An interim reparations plan, the Dawes Plan, emerged from the London conference of July–August 1924. ... France was obliged to evacuate the Ruhr (by August 1925), to end sanctions on the Rhine, and to promise never again to impose sanctions on Germany without the unanimous agreement of the Reparations Commission. The United States would lend $200,000,000 to Germany to "prime the pump," and Germany would pay from 1,000,000,000 to 2,500,000,000 marks in reparations for five years.

fact: 1924年2月1日英国承认苏联，2月开始谈判英苏条约（包括贸易条约和处理沙俄时期英国债券持有人问题的条约）。但条约在保守党和自由党中引发强烈反对，9月围绕对苏贷款的争论使谈判几乎破裂。「坎贝尔案」（政府撤销对左翼报纸《工人周刊》编辑坎贝尔煽动叛乱罪的起诉）成为保守党攻击麦克唐纳的把柄。

sources.title: Wikipedia, 1924 in the Soviet Union
sources.quote: 1 February – United Kingdom recognized the Soviet Union

sources.title: Biography Guide, Ramsay MacDonald
sources.quote: MacDonald recognised the Soviet Union and informed Parliament in February 1924 that negotiations would begin to negotiate a treaty with the Soviet Union. ... The treaties were popular neither with the Conservatives nor with the Liberals, who, in September, criticised the loan so vehemently that negotiation with them seemed impossible. However, the government's fate was determined by the "Campbell Case", the abrogation of prosecuting the left-wing newspaper the Workers' Weekly for inciting servicemen to mutiny.

fact: 1924年10月8日，英国下议院就坎贝尔案进行不信任投票，以364票对199票通过对政府的谴责动议（自由党加入保守党投票反对政府）。麦克唐纳随即向乔治五世国王辞职，首届工党政府结束。10月底大选前夕，《每日邮报》公布了所谓的「季诺维也夫信件」（共产国际主席季诺维也夫致英国共产党的信，号召革命活动），信件真伪至今有争议，但被认为影响了选举结果。

sources.title: Grokipedia, 1924 Labour Government
sources.quote: On October 8, 1924, the House of Commons voted 364 to 199 in favor of the censure motion, with the Liberal Party joining the Conservatives in voting against the government. The defeat was a devastating blow, and Macdonald immediately tendered his resignation to King George V. ... The Zinoviev Letter, a purported communication from Grigory Zinoviev, head of the Communist International, to the Communist Party of Great Britain, calling for revolutionary activity. The letter, published by the Daily Mail and the Foreign Office, was widely believed to have influenced the election result, though its authenticity has been debated by historians ever since.

fact: 1924年工党政府通过了《惠特利住宅法》（Wheatley Housing Act），由卫生大臣约翰·惠特利推动，大幅增加政府对地方当局建造市政公屋的补贴，面向低收入工人。该法被视为两次世界大战之间最重要的社会立法之一，到1933年推动建造了超过50万套新住宅。

sources.title: Grokipedia, 1924 Labour Government
sources.quote: One of the most significant legislative achievements of the 1924 Labour Government was the Wheatley Housing Act, named after John Wheatley, the Minister of Health. The Act provided subsidies to local authorities for the construction of council housing, aiming to address the severe housing shortage that had developed during and after World War I. The Wheatley Housing Act is widely regarded as one of the most important pieces of social legislation of the interwar period, leading to the construction of over 500,000 new homes by 1933.

sources.title: MasteryMind, A-Level History: Wars and Welfare
sources.quote: One landmark housing act was passed by John Wheatley during the 1924 First Labour Government: The Wheatley Housing Act of 1924, which provided increased government subsidies to local authorities to build rentable council housing.

fact: 1924年英国经济处于战后恢复期，市场普遍预期英镑将回归金本位。财政大臣斯诺登是金本位的坚定拥护者，但1924年内尚未正式实施。1925年4月丘吉尔推动恢复战前英镑黄金兑换比价（1英镑=4.86美元），5月14日《1925年金本位法案》生效。凯恩斯曾警告英镑被高估约10%，将重创出口行业。

sources.title: MasteryMind, A-Level History: Wars and Welfare
sources.quote: The return to the Gold Standard at $4.86 was not the sole cause, but it acted as the critical economic catalyst. By overvaluing sterling, it made British coal uncompetitive abroad. ... Chancellor of the Exchequer Winston Churchill, advised by Bank of England Governor Montagu Norman, sought to restore London's traditional pre-eminence as the financial capital of the world. They believed returning to the historic parity of $4.86 would restore international business confidence, despite warnings from economists like John Maynard Keynes that it overvalued the pound by 10%.

sources.title: Wikiwand，切爾文券（英国金本位段落）
sources.quote: 1925年4月,英國財政大臣邱吉爾推動恢復戰前的英鎊黃金兌換比價,重回金本位,將英鎊和美元的匯率恢復至1:4.86金平價水平。英國議會通過了《1925年金本位法案》,5月14日英國國王簽署法案並生效。

fact: 道威斯计划的资金循环：美国银行向德国放贷→德国工业恢复→德国向英法支付赔款→英法向美国偿还战债。伦敦城作为国际金融中心，承销对德贷款和赔款相关债券。1920—1931年德国赔款总支出230亿马克，其中125亿为现金（主要来自纽约银行贷款），其余为煤炭、化工品和铁路设备等实物。德国从贷款中获得的资金超过了它实际支付的赔款。

sources.title: Wikipedia, Weimar Republic
sources.quote: The total reparations payout from 1920 to 1931 (when payments were suspended indefinitely) was 23 billion marks. 12.5 billion was cash that came mostly from loans provided by New York bankers. The rest was goods such as coal and chemicals, or from assets like railway equipment.

sources.title: GRO Learning, Stresemann and the Recovery of Germany, 1924–1929
sources.quote: This created a circular flow: American loans → German industrial recovery → reparations paid to France and Britain → Allied war debts repaid to America. The plan worked while American prosperity lasted. When the Wall Street Crash ended US lending in 1929, the whole structure collapsed.

fact: 1924年工党政府扩大了失业保险覆盖面并提高了失业救济金，但受财政正统主义（平衡预算、金本位）限制。煤矿补贴和失业救济制度是1920年代英国社会政策的核心。1924年的英国仍是议会民主制，工党首次执政证明了「民主宪政社会主义」的可行性，没有引发革命性动荡。

sources.title: Grokipedia, 1924 Labour Government
sources.quote: The government also took steps to address the chronic unemployment that plagued the British economy in the 1920s. Labour expanded unemployment insurance coverage and increased benefits for the unemployed, though these measures were constrained by the government's limited financial resources and its commitment to fiscal orthodoxy. Philip Snowden, as Chancellor of the Exchequer, was a staunch advocate of balanced budgets and the gold standard, which limited the scope for expansive public spending.

sources.title: MasteryMind, A-Level History
sources.quote: The 1924 Labour Government was profoundly significant because it normalised democratic constitutional socialism, disproved fears that Labour would spark revolutionary disorder, and decisively relegated the Liberal Party to third-party status in British politics.

fact: 1920年代英国经济面临结构性困难：煤矿业设备陈旧、资本投资不足、来自波兰和美国煤矿的竞争、德国赔款煤炭交付冲击市场。1924年金本位回归预期使英镑面临升值压力，出口行业（尤其煤炭）竞争力受损。伦敦城的金融服务业是英国经济的支柱，但传统制造业持续衰退。

sources.title: MasteryMind, A-Level History
sources.quote: Contrast the Gold Standard with deep-rooted structural economic weaknesses, including outdated machinery, lack of capital investment, German reparations coal deliveries, and international competition from Polish and American mines.

sources.title: Grokipedia, 1924 Labour Government
sources.quote: Philip Snowden, as Chancellor of the Exchequer, was a staunch advocate of balanced budgets and the gold standard, which limited the scope for expansive public spending. This tension between Labour's reformist ambitions and the constraints of economic orthodoxy would become a recurring theme in the party's history.

fact: 1920年代英国的失业率持续偏高，即使在最好年份失业人口仍在130万左右。1924年工党政府扩大失业保险覆盖并提高救济金，但财政正统主义限制了支出规模。伦敦的生活成本在战后逐步稳定，但传统工业区（威尔士、苏格兰、英格兰北部）的贫困和失业问题严重。

sources.title: GRO Learning, Stresemann and the Recovery of Germany
sources.quote: High unemployment - Even during the best years, unemployment hovered around 1.3 million, indicating that prosperity did not reach all sections of society.

sources.title: Grokipedia, 1924 Labour Government
sources.quote: Labour expanded unemployment insurance coverage and increased benefits for the unemployed, though these measures were constrained by the government's limited financial resources and its commitment to fiscal orthodoxy.
